title: Domains and Ranges of Transformations of a Function f on [0, 2]
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The accompanying figure shows the graph of a function f(x) with domain [0, 2] and range [0, 1] (an arch starting at (0, 0), peaking at (1, 1), and ending at (2, 0)). Find the domains and ranges of the following functions: (a) f(x) + 2, (b) f(x) - 1, (c) 2f(x), (d) -f(x), (e) f(x + 2), (f) f(x - 1), (g) f(-x), and (h) -f(x + 1) + 1.

steps.title: Analyze Vertical Transformations in Parts (a), (b), (c), and (d)
steps.explanation: Vertical shifts, stretches, and x-axis reflections do not alter the inputs x, so the domain remains [0, 2] in parts (a)-(d), while the range [0, 1] is shifted up 2 in (a), shifted down 1 in (b), stretched by 2 in (c), and negated to [-1, 0] in (d).
steps.why: Operations applied outside f(x) transform the y-coordinates (range) while leaving the x-coordinates (domain) unchanged.

steps.title: Analyze Horizontal Transformations in Parts (e), (f), and (g)
steps.mathExpression: \begin{aligned} \text{(e) } f(x + 2) &: 0 \le x + 2 \le 2 \implies D = [-2, 0], \quad R = [0, 1] \\ \text{(f) } f(x - 1) &: 0 \le x - 1 \le 2 \implies D = [1, 3], \quad R = [0, 1] \\ \text{(g) } f(-x) &: 0 \le -x \le 2 \implies D = [-2, 0], \quad R = [0, 1] \end{aligned}
steps.explanation: Pure horizontal translations and y-axis reflections leave the set of y-values unchanged at R = [0, 1], while shifting the domain [0, 2] left 2 to [-2, 0] in (e), right 1 to [1, 3] in (f), and reflecting across x = 0 to [-2, 0] in (g).
steps.why: The argument inside f(...) must lie in the original domain [0, 2].

steps.title: Analyze the Combined Transformation in Part (h)
steps.explanation: For -f(x + 1) + 1, requiring 0 <= x + 1 <= 2 shifts the domain left 1 unit to [-1, 1]. Vertically, negating the range [0, 1] gives [-1, 0], and adding 1 shifts it back to [0, 1] (an inverted arch with endpoints (-1, 1), (1, 1) and minimum (0, 0)).
steps.why: Horizontal operations transform the domain and vertical operations transform the range independently.
